faqs.a: Egress is data leaving the cloud provider's network to the internet - every download, stream, or API response your users receive. Ingress (uploads into the cloud) is usually free. Providers charge for egress because backbone bandwidth costs them real money.

Typical list prices are around $0.09/GB for the first 10 TB/month on major clouds, dropping with volume tiers. Some providers charge $0.12+/GB, while flat-fee hosts and R2-style storage charge $0. Egress is often the single largest line item on a cloud bill.
faqs.q: What does egress usually cost per GB?

faqs.a: Use a CDN: cached content is served from the edge, often at far lower per-GB rates or free tiers. Compress images and video, enable caching headers, and consider providers with free egress for the same-region or CDN-served traffic.
faqs.q: How can I reduce egress costs?

faqs.a: Ingress - uploading data into the cloud - is free on virtually all major providers. Transfers between services in the same region are usually free too. Egress charges apply when data leaves to the internet or to another region.

Cloudflare R2 famously charges $0 for egress, which is why it is popular for download-heavy workloads. But compare total cost: storage, operations, and compute pricing differ, and migration has its own cost. This calculator lets you model any rate, including $0.
faqs.q: Is R2 really free for egress?

faqs.a: A 2-hour HD movie stream is roughly 3 GB. At $0.09/GB that is about $0.27 per viewer just in bandwidth. One million views costs around $270,000 in egress alone - which is exactly why streaming economics depend on CDNs and peering deals.
faqs.q: What does streaming cost in egress?

cloud-egress-cost-calculator.formula:
Billable GB = max(0, monthly GB - free tier GB).
Monthly cost = billable GB x price per GB.
Yearly cost = monthly cost x 12.
Effective per GB = monthly cost / monthly GB.
Example: (12,288 - 100) x 0.09 = $1,096.92/month.
howTo: Enter your monthly data transfer out in GB.
Enter the provider's free tier in GB (0 if there is none).
Enter the per-GB egress price from the provider's pricing page.
Read your monthly and yearly cost plus the effective per-GB rate.
Try different providers' rates to compare the real cost of switching.

cloud-egress-cost-calculator.workedExample:
12,288 GB/month, 100 GB free tier, $0.09/GB:
1. Billable GB = 12,288 - 100 = 12,188 GB.
2. Monthly cost = 12,188 x 0.09 = $1,096.92.
3. Yearly cost = 1,096.92 x 12 = $13,163.04.
4. Effective per GB = 1,096.92 / 12,288 = $0.0893.
At $0/GB (R2-style), the same transfer costs $0 - which is why provider choice matters.
